title: Man. Post. Cap. II §XIV: Garissoles 2 / Placeus — in ipso contradiction invented
pass_a_gloss: GAR. 2. How can these things be composed among themselves? Adam's sin is imputed to us, not as it stuck in him, and Adam's sin is imputed to us as it was permanent viciousness in him: for to stick in Adam, and to be permanent in Adam, what they differ here, I indeed do not see. PLAC. The proposition, Adam's sin is imputed to us, not as it stuck in him, is indeed mine; but the opposite to it, Adam's sin is imputed to us as it was permanent viciousness in him, is not mine. For the words in him, which make the contradiction, he did not find in my writings, but the learned Man added from his own at this place: nor indeed do they appear in the exposition of my opinion which he himself had set forth beforehand in § x. Therefore that contradiction he himself made and invented, and falsely attributed to me.
pass_b_english: Garissoles: (2) How can these be reconciled? "Adam's sin is imputed to us not as it stuck in him," and "Adam's sin is imputed to us as it was lasting viciousness in him"—for what difference is there here between "sticking in Adam" and "being lasting in Adam"? I do not see. Placeus: The proposition "Adam's sin is imputed to us not as it stuck in him" is mine; the opposite, "Adam's sin is imputed to us as it was lasting viciousness in him," is not. The words "in him," which create the contradiction, he did not find in my writings; the learned man added them here from his own stock. Nor do they appear in the exposition of my view that he himself had set out earlier in §x. So he made and invented that contradiction and falsely pinned it on me.
source_text:
GAR. 2. Quomodo ista componi possunt inter se? Peccatum Adae imputatur nobis, non qua haesit in ipso, & peccatum Adae imputatur nobis qua fuit vitiositas permanens in ipso: nam haerere in Adamo, & esse permanens in Adamo, quid hic differant, ego quidem non video.

PLAC. Propositio, Peccatum Adae imputatur nobis, non qua haesit in ipso, mea quidem est; sed illi opposita, Peccatum Adae imputatur nobis qua fuit vitiositas permanens in ipso, mea non est. Voces enim in ipso, quae contradictionem efficiunt, non invenit in meis scriptis, sed de suo Vir doctus addidit hoc loco: neque vero illae comparent in sententiae meae expositione quam ipse praemiserat § x. Contradictionem igitur istam ipse fecit ac finxit, mihique falso tribuit.
